newsitem.title: USA: Littlefield needs funds, sales to survive.
newsitem.headline: Littlefield needs funds, sales to survive.

text.p: Littlefield, Adams & Co, reporting a net loss amid an 85 percent drop in product sales in the second quarter, said Thursday it needed more funds or sales to remain in business.

"Without the generation of additional sales or the procurement of additional funds through new borrowings ..., it is likely the company will not have sufficient cash flows to maintain itself after the 1997 third quarter," a company statement said.
Littlefield posted a $699,000 net loss, or $0.25 a share, in the second quarter ended June 30, compared with a $340,000 profit, or $0.15 a share. in the 1996 quarter.
Quarterly product sales plummeted 85 percent to $450,000 from $3.0 million in the 1996 quarter. In the first half, product sales contracted to $1.8 million, from $6.4 million in the 1996 period.
The company attributed the drop to the expiration of its Harley-Davidson license on December 31 1996. It added $699,000 of Harley-Davidson sales are included in the 1997 first half figures.
The company said it currently can meet its obligations, but warned that could change after the third quarter, unless its new products are successful.
"These factors raise substantial doubts concerning the ability of the company to continue as a going concern," the company statement said.
The company's stock closed at 3/4 Wednesday, close to its 52-week low of 9/16.
